outcome: Neonatal complications (transient tachypnea of the newborn, respiratory distress, admission to the neonatal unit)
cohort: 3150 women with singleton pregnancy undergoing planned cesarean delivery between 37 0/7 and 41 6/7 weeks' gestation
finding: While neonatal acidosis was more common in planned cesarean deliveries with sustained spinal hypotension and prolonged anesthesia-to-incision and incision-to-delivery intervals, serious perinatal consequences were rare.
